problems: 'The compiler registration pointed at the wrong location' is stated as fact; the maintainer only said there might be an issue with the installation paths
cause_fixed: With CMSIS-Toolbox 2.4.0 the compiler check ran armclang without a target; with 2.9.0 the target was passed but the check still failed. fix_fixed: Update the toolbox, check the setup with `cbuild list environment` and `cbuild list toolchains -v`, and use the regular Arm Compiler 6.22 instead of the FuSa variant unless an MDK Professional licence is available.

cause_fixed: The csolution.yml still set compiler: AC6 while CubeMX was set to generate for the STM32CubeIDE toolchain (GCC).

problems: 'Nightly of December 2024' is not in the thread, which only links a nightly run 'from last night'
cause_fixed: cbuild 2.6.1 did not pass the -g and -O compile options to files placed in nested sub-groups, so no debug info was produced and breakpoints could not be set.
fix_fixed: Use a CMSIS-Toolbox nightly with the fix, which the reporter confirmed; no release is named. Until then keep such files out of nested groups.

problems: '--context-set (what the VS Code build button does)' is misleading: the reporter says the button runs --context-set together with --context, and then the execute does not run
cause_fixed: executes nodes are only processed on full application builds; --context builds one project only, and for-context is only valid in cproject files (solution-level executes run once).
fix_fixed: Build with --context-set but without --context, or without any context option. Place execute nodes in the cproject.yml when they must run per context with for-context.

problems: 'Tokenised by the generator' is not given as the mechanism in the thread
'A newer CMake accepts the form' is not in the thread; the reporter only said his CMake (^3.25.2) seemed happy with it
The maintainer's point that CMake drops function-style definitions with a warning is left out
cause_fixed: Without escaping or inner quotes the function-like define is split into separate -D tokens. Quoted forms reach the generated CMakeLists.txt intact, but CMake may then drop function-style definitions with a warning.
fix_fixed: Escape the characters (e.g. _LIBCPP_VERBOSE_ABORT\(\.\.\.\): \(\(void\)0\)) or use YAML quoting that keeps the inner quotes, e.g. - '"NAME(...)=((void)0)"'. The reporter's CMake (^3.25.2) accepted the macro; where CMake drops it, define the macro in a header file.

problems: Verifying with cbuild list toolchains is not in the thread
cause_fixed: CMake falls back to a gcc from PATH if the compiler is not registered.
fix_fixed: Register the compiler with the environment variable GCC_TOOLCHAIN_<major>_<minor>_<patch> holding the absolute path to its bin directory (Toolchain Registration); another user fixed it by correcting the path and environment variables.

problems: '2023 toolbox' is not in the thread
cause_fixed: The AS_ARM language used for legacy armasm files had no link rule in the AC6 CMake description, so linking produced no .axf and reported no error.
fix_fixed: Fixed in devtools PR 1101; the workaround was appending a CMAKE_AS_ARM_LINK_EXECUTABLE armlink rule to the AC6.<version>.cmake file.

problems: Resolution 'fixed-in-release' is not supported: the maintainers only asked the reporter to check PR #284, with no confirmation or release
That PR #284 falls back to the attribute is only inferred from a plan to test __has_attribute
cause_fixed: For IAR the macro maps to the C11 _Noreturn keyword (since CMSIS_6 PR #85), which is not allowed in a function pointer type.
fix_fixed: Use __attribute__((__noreturn__)) directly in the typedef (needs language extensions on IAR). The maintainers planned to use the attribute when __has_attribute reports it and asked the reporter to check PR #284; no confirmation in the thread.

problems: 'Armv7-M where TBLOFF spans bits 29:7' contradicts the thread: the CMSIS mask covers bits 31:7, and bits 29:7 is the restriction an implementer such as ST may choose
cause_fixed: CMSIS implements VTOR.TBLOFF as the Armv7-M architecture specifies it (mask 0xFFFFFF80); implementers such as ST may restrict the implemented bits and require stronger alignment (512 bytes on this STM32).
fix_fixed: Align the vector table as the device manual requires; CMSIS cannot encode implementation specifics.

problems: Version 6.0.0 is not in the thread
No CMSIS_6 release with PR #141 is named; the thread only shows the PR being created and extra GCC warnings added in #140
cause_fixed: A clang pragma was left in the GCC header cmsis_gcc.h, which GCC rejects under -Werror=unknown-pragmas.
fix_fixed: Replace it with `#pragma GCC system_header` in cmsis_gcc.h, as proposed in PR #141; no merge or release is shown.

problems: What PR #122 changes (keeping the old name) is not in the thread, which only says 'Addressed by #122'

fix_fixed: Use DCB_Type; the issue was marked as addressed by PR #122 without saying what it changes or which release has it.
versions_fixed: CMSIS 5.9 defines CoreDebug_Type; CMSIS 6.0 renamed it
